clue.text: Wanting time to make up a deficit

parts.note: wanting, as in lacking, means short
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: Someone trying to cover a financial gap by waiting it out.
explanation.definitionFit: A deficit is an amount by which something falls short, the same as a lack in supply.

clue.text: Master of vessel expected

parts.note: a sub is a submarine, a type of vessel
due means expected, as in a train that is due

explanation.surface: The captain of a ship is about to arrive.
explanation.definitionFit: To master something is to overcome or bring it under control, just as to subdue it.

clue.text: It may be buttonholed or rebuked

parts.note: chid is an old past tense of chide, to scold or rebuke

explanation.surface: Someone is either cornered for a chat or told off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'buttonholed' suggests being detained in conversation; here it means worn in a buttonhole.
explanation.definitionFit: A showy flower such as this is often worn as a buttonhole at weddings.

clue.text: So the judge introduces alternative final sentence

indicators.note: the judge comes in front of the remaining pieces, leading them

parts.note: a ref, or referee, judges a match
or introduces an alternative

indicators.note: only the last letter of the word sentence is used

explanation.surface: A judge delivers an alternative closing sentence in court.
explanation.definitionFit: Therefore and so both mean for that reason, introducing a consequence.

clue.text: Happy to give duo more dough

indicators.note: give in the sense of bend or yield, so the letters lose their shape

explanation.surface: A cheerful benefactor hands a pair of performers a pay rise.
explanation.definitionFit: Being good-humoured means being cheerful and amiable, so happy is a fair synonym.

clue.text: Beat decisively in a field event

definitions.meaning: to beat an opponent heavily, as in thrashing them
the athletics throwing event with a weighted ball on a wire

explanation.surface: An athlete wins convincingly at a throwing competition.
explanation.definitionFit: To trounce someone is a colloquial sense of the verb, and the athletics throw with a ball on a wire bears the same name.

clue.text: A body of gunmen turned on him

indicators.note: turned means the abbreviation for the gunners is read the other way round

parts.note: RA is the Royal Artillery, the British army's gunners

explanation.surface: A gang of armed men attacked a man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned on' looks like 'attacked'; 'turned' reverses RA and ON is taken as written. 'him' is a man, the biblical brother of Moses.
explanation.definitionFit: A man's name serves as an example for the pronoun, here the biblical high priest.

clue.text: Formidable chaps giving outstanding service

parts.note: chaps are men
in tennis, acing is serving an unreturnable ball

explanation.surface: Impressive men delivering superb service, perhaps as waiters.
explanation.definitionFit: Something menacing is threatening and frightening, which is what formidable means.

clue.text: When drowsy I'm disturbed by noisy behaviour

indicators.note: being disturbed means thrown into disorder, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A sleepy person complains about rowdy neighbours keeping them awake.
explanation.definitionFit: Rowdyism is rough, loud and disorderly conduct, as of rowdy people.

clue.text: One would lose status as a union member

definitions.text: One would lose status as a union member

parts.words: One would lose status as a union member
parts.note: the union is marriage, not a trade union: an unmarried man gives up his single status on becoming a partner in it

explanation.surface: A worker who would be stripped of standing by joining a trade union.
explanation.walkthrough: 'union member' suggests a trade union; the union meant is a marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: An unmarried man loses that single status the moment he becomes one half of a married couple.

clue.text: This has been used poetically in the past

definitions.text: This has been used poetically in the past

parts.words: This has been used poetically in the past
parts.note: a poetic, archaic word meaning before the present time, which is what 'in the past' itself means

explanation.surface: A comment on some word that poets once favoured.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the past' works twice over: the word was used in older poetry, and it means 'before now'.
explanation.definitionFit: The archaic poetic adverb means 'before this time', which is a way of saying in the past.

clue.text: Equipment used in the services

parts.note: 'services' suggests the armed forces, but means serves in a ball game played over a net

explanation.surface: Kit issued to the armed forces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the services' reads as the army, navy and air force; here it means serves in a match.
explanation.definitionFit: A strung bat used to hit a ball, including when serving, at Wimbledon and the like.

clue.text: Join some troops heading east

indicators.note: the troops lead, coming ahead of the compass point

parts.note: a unit is a body of soldiers

explanation.surface: An invitation to enlist with a detachment marching eastwards.
explanation.definitionFit: To unite is to join together, a direct synonym of the verb.

clue.text: Loud clamour may lead to apprehension

definitions.meaning: a public outcry or noisy protest
historically the shout raised by citizens pursuing a criminal, leading to the arrest of the wrongdoer

explanation.surface: Noisy shouting that makes people nervous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'apprehension' looks like anxiety; it is arrest, as in the old English duty to raise the alarm and chase a felon.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means a public outcry, and originally the alarm raised to pursue and capture a criminal.

clue.text: Moses received them in order, ten set out in writing

definitions.text: Moses received them in order, ten set out in writing

parts.words: Moses received them in order, ten set out in writing
parts.note: the biblical laws handed to Moses on Mount Sinai, ten of them, inscribed on stone tablets; 'in order' hints that each is an instruction

explanation.surface: Moses was given ten written rules, neatly listed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in order' reads as 'arranged', but each item is an order, an instruction from God.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ten Commandments were the laws given by God to Moses on tablets of stone.

clue.text: It was spliced with spirit

parts.note: the naval order to splice this rope meant issuing an extra ration of rum, the spirit

explanation.surface: Something joined with gusto.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spirit' looks like enthusiasm; it is rum, issued when the navy gave the order to splice the main brace.
explanation.definitionFit: A principal rope on a sailing ship; 'splice the main brace' became the order for a celebratory rum ration.

clue.text: Ruins runaway affairs on ship

definitions.meaning: wrecks or thwarts, as in sinking a plan
openings in a ship's side that let water run away off the deck

explanation.surface: Romantic flings at sea come to grief.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runaway affairs' looks like elopements; the second sense is drains that let water run away.
explanation.definitionFit: To scupper a plan is to wreck it, and scuppers are also deck drains on a vessel.

clue.text: Allow real change in a better system

indicators.note: the rearranged word goes inside the betting system

parts.note: the tote is a betting system, for punters, or betters

indicators.note: change means the letters of real are altered in order

explanation.surface: A reform of a better system is permitted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' turns REAL into LERA, which goes inside TOTE. 'better' is one who bets, not 'superior'.
explanation.definitionFit: To tolerate is to put up with or permit something, so allow is a direct synonym.

clue.text: In this one is right behind someone with a private hobby

definitions.text: In this one is right behind

parts.note: close can mean secretive or private, as in a close person
a pursuit is a pastime or hobby

explanation.surface: Someone with a secret pastime is being followed closely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'someone with' is a link: such a person has a private hobby, a phrase that splits into the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: When a chase is close, the pursuer is right on the heels of the one being followed.

clue.text: Port doesn't open to give shelter

indicators.note: the word for a port loses its opening letter

parts.note: a harbour is a port

explanation.surface: A port that will not open its gates to ships needing refuge.
explanation.definitionFit: An arbour is a shady garden retreat formed by trees or climbing plants, a kind of shelter.

clue.text: What consumers want to ask?

definitions.meaning: in economics, the desire of buyers for goods

explanation.surface: Wondering what shoppers would like to request.
explanation.definitionFit: Demand is the economic term for consumers' desire for goods, and as a verb it means to ask forcefully.

clue.text: Wonders when phone is out of order and name has changed

indicators.note: a broken telephone suggests its letters are jumbled into a new arrangement
the name being altered signals its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Marvelling that the phone is broken and someone's name has been altered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is out of order' rearranges PHONE into PHENO; 'has changed' rearranges NAME into MENA.
explanation.definitionFit: Phenomena are remarkable occurrences or marvels, so wonders is a fair plural synonym.

clue.text: It's obvious the minister was brought up in the Old Testament

indicators.note: the reversed title is placed within the testament abbreviation

parts.note: OT is the abbreviation for the Old Testament

indicators.note: in a down clue, brought up means read from bottom to top, reversing

parts.note: Rev, short for Reverend, is a minister's title

explanation.surface: A minister was clearly raised on the Old Testament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought up' turns REV into VER, which sits inside OT.
explanation.definitionFit: Overt means open and plainly seen, so obvious is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Carried north in a tidal wave

indicators.note: the letter for north is placed within the word for the wave

parts.note: a bore is a surge of tide up an estuary, like the Severn Bore

explanation.surface: Something swept north by a huge tidal wave.
explanation.walkthrough: A bore is a tidal wave running up a river, famously the Severn Bore in England.
explanation.definitionFit: Borne is the past participle of bear, meaning carried or transported.

clue.text: Gloss over title in the Spanish style

indicators.note: the Spanish article covers the title, wrapping round it on both sides

parts.note: el is the Spanish word for the
a title is a name

explanation.surface: Advice to skip over a heading written in a Spanish manner.
explanation.definitionFit: Enamel is a glossy coating, and a gloss is likewise a shiny finish or paint.

clue.text: State accepted initially leaving Omaha out

parts.note: OK means approved or accepted

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the word leaving is taken
out signals the city name is put out of its usual order

explanation.surface: A US state was approved for travel, but the route skipped the city of Omaha.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges OMAHA into AHOMA; 'leaving Omaha out' looks like a deletion, but nothing is removed.
explanation.definitionFit: Oklahoma is one of the fifty United States, so it is an example of a state.

clue.text: The rest of the afternoon

parts.note: 'rest' is a nap, not the remainder: a sleep taken in the early afternoon, especially in hot countries

explanation.surface: What remains of the day after lunch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rest' seems to mean the remainder; it means a nap.
explanation.definitionFit: A siesta is a short sleep after the midday meal, an afternoon rest in warm countries.

clue.text: The elder made king of England

indicators.note: made in the sense of fashioned anew, so the letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: An older man was crowned English monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethelred the Unready was an Anglo-Saxon ruler of England around the year 1000.
